gloss: a bit more; somewhat more; on the larger side

definitions.gloss: a bit more; somewhat more; on the larger side
definitions.explanation: An amount or quantity that is slightly larger than usual or than what is strictly required. The suffix め attaches to adjectives or quantity words to mean 'on the X side.'

examples.japanese: ご{飯|はん}を{多|おお}めに{盛|も}る。
{塩|しお}を{多|おお}めに{入|い}れてください。
examples.english: Please add a little more salt.

examples.japanese: {週末|しゅうまつ}は{客|きゃく}が{増|ふ}えるので、{食材|しょくざい}を{多|おお}めに{仕入|しい}れておいた。
examples.english: Since customers increase on weekends, I stocked up on a bit more ingredients.

notes:
Formed from {多|おお}い (many, much) + the suffix め (tendency toward, slightly on the X side). Most often used adverbially as {多|おお}めに.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {多|おお}めに{入|い}れる: put in a bit more
- {多|おお}めに{作|つく}る: make a bit more
- {多|おお}めに{見積|みつ}もる: estimate on the high side
- {多|おお}めの{量|りょう}: a somewhat larger amount

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {少|すく}なめ: a bit less — the opposite, used in the same way
- たっぷり: plenty; a lot — emphasizes generous quantity, stronger than {多|おお}め
- {大|おお}きめ: a bit larger (in size) — uses め with size rather than quantity

cross_references.label: a bit early, on the early side
